findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:0 verificationEvidence overclaims selfcheck coverage. The note states "selfcheck: an out-of-ws Edit tool-event whose input.new_string carries a PEM private key => secretScan true (Edit content harvested)" but live-engine-selfcheck.mjs contains no corresponding assertion. The only Edit-tool test (benignOutOfWsEdit, line 148) uses benign content and checks forbiddenPath/forbiddenCreate, not secretScan. There is no stub behavior or ok()/eq() call that injects a PEM key via an Edit new_string and asserts secretScan=true. The evidence note uses the selfcheck: prefix without a matching selfcheck assertion, making this a gap between stated and actual coverage for a high-risk must intent.

CHK-002:edge:1 verificationEvidence overclaims selfcheck coverage. The note states "selfcheck: an out-of-ws NotebookEdit whose cell source (new_source/source) carries a secret => secretScan true (notebook content harvested)" but live-engine-selfcheck.mjs has no such assertion. The only NotebookEdit test (benignOutOfWsNotebookEdit, line 150) uses benign cell source and checks forbiddenPath/forbiddenCreate only. There is no stub behavior or ok()/eq() call that injects a secret value via NotebookEdit new_source and asserts secretScan=true. The evidence note prefix 'selfcheck:' implies a passing assertion that does not exist.

CHK-002:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence overclaims selfcheck coverage. The note states "selfcheck: a secret split across multiple tool events => at least the complete-pattern event trips secretScan (each event content is accumulated into newContent across the cell history)" but live-engine-selfcheck.mjs contains no split-secret test case. There is no stub behavior, no multi-event tool_use message array with partial AKIA fragments, and no ok()/eq() call asserting that a split secret triggers secretScan. The content accumulation code at live-engine.mjs lines 648-694 is real, but no selfcheck assertion exercises the specific multi-event split-secret scenario stated in the intent.
